Kitchen Remodeling in Augusta, KS

Augusta is Butler County's largest city, with approximately 9,300 residents and a median household income that reflects the community's established blue-collar and professional base. The Wheatland River and Dry Walnut Creek run through Augusta's eastern reaches, and the housing stock along the downtown oil-era grid tells the history of a city that boomed in the 1910s and built steadily through the 1970s.

Augusta is Butler County's largest city and its kitchens cover the full range of Butler County housing history — from oil-era homes near the downtown grid with original cabinetry and layouts that haven't changed since the 1940s, to mid-century ranches on the west side that were built when Augusta was growing, to newer subdivision homes off Highway 400 with 1990s builder kitchens now showing their age. Each vintage has its own set of problems and its own remodel story.

Wheatland Construction is Butler County based and serves Augusta regularly. We're a Veterans Approved Builder (ID: 00899), Home Advisor Certified since 2019, and family-owned since 2018. We've worked in Augusta's older housing stock and we know what 80-year-old kitchens actually need versus what they can get away with.

Augusta Kitchen Remodel by Housing Era

Pre-1950s homes near downtown: These kitchens were designed for a different era of cooking — smaller, separate from dining, often with original steel cabinets or early wood construction. The plumbing configuration, electrical (often still knob-and-tube or early 2-wire), and structural framing all need to be assessed before pricing a remodel. These projects take more planning than a suburban refresh but the character these homes have is worth doing right.

Mid-century ranches (1950s–1970s): The most common Augusta kitchen remodel candidate. Original layouts, galley configurations, cabinets at end of life, countertops long past their prime. Open-concept conversions are popular here — removing the wall between the kitchen and the dining or living area transforms how the first floor functions.

1980s–2000s subdivisions west and east of Augusta: Builder-grade kitchens hitting 20–40 year milestones. Particle-board cabinet boxes, laminate countertops with failed seams, inadequate ventilation. The fix is more straightforward than the older homes — it's a quality replacement job rather than a full gut.

What We Build in Augusta Kitchens

  • Full gut renovations for older downtown-area homes — new layout, plumbing update, electrical assessment, proper ventilation, custom or semi-custom cabinets, quartz or granite countertops
  • Open-concept conversions — structural assessment, wall removal, beam installation, permit through City of Augusta or Butler County, coordinated flooring transition
  • Mid-range refreshes — cabinet replacement or refacing, countertop upgrade, backsplash, lighting update, new fixtures
  • Appliance coordination — exterior-vented range hood installation, dishwasher, range as part of the broader scope

Permits in Augusta

City of Augusta Building Department for homes inside city limits. Butler County for unincorporated properties outside city limits. We determine jurisdiction and handle all permits.

How We Approach Kitchen Remodeling in Augusta

Every kitchen remodel starts with a site visit. We measure the existing layout, look at the plumbing rough-in and drain stack location, check the electrical panel for capacity, and assess structural walls before discussing what's possible. We price in writing with every line item documented.

Our crew handles demo through final walkthrough. Cabinet delivery, tile setting, countertop templating, plumbing trim-out, electrical, and final inspection all coordinated through us - no handoffs to subcontractors who don't know the project.

Wheatland Construction has held Veterans Approved Builder status (ID: 00899) since we opened and has been Home Advisor Certified since 2019. We're licensed and insured in Kansas.

In Augusta, the diverse housing stock - oil-era downtown homes, mid-century ranches, Highway 400 subdivisions - means every project gets an honest vintage assessment before scoping begins.

Frequently Asked Questions About Kitchen Remodeling in Augusta

How much does kitchen remodeling cost in Augusta, KS?

Augusta kitchen remodels range from $18,000 for a mid-range refresh to $80,000+ for a full gut renovation on an older downtown home with plumbing and electrical updates. Mid-century ranch open-concept conversions typically run $30,000–$55,000. Written, line-item estimates on every project.

Do older Augusta homes need special consideration for kitchen remodeling?

Yes. Pre-1950s homes near downtown Augusta may have original electrical (knob-and-tube or early 2-wire), lead pipes, or plaster walls that need to be addressed during a kitchen remodel. We assess all of this before pricing — no surprises after demo starts.

Who handles permits for kitchen remodeling in Augusta?

City of Augusta Building Department for homes inside city limits. Butler County for unincorporated properties. We determine the correct jurisdiction and handle all permit work.

How long does a kitchen renovation take in Augusta?

6–12 weeks depending on scope. Older homes with more complex plumbing and electrical work take longer. We give you a realistic timeline in the estimate.

Can you do an open-concept kitchen conversion in an older Augusta ranch home?

Yes — this is one of the most common projects we do in mid-century Augusta homes. We assess whether the wall is load-bearing, quote the structural work and beam if required, pull the permit, and handle the full scope.

What countertop and cabinet materials do you recommend for Augusta kitchens?

Quartz countertops for durability and maintenance. Plywood-box cabinets with solid wood or MDF door fronts for longevity. In older Augusta homes with more character, custom or semi-custom cabinets that match the home's style work better than stock builder-grade.
